# GPIO ALLOCATION - ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N8R2

Pin numbers and alternate functions are from the *ESP32-S3-WROOM-1 & WROOM-1U Datasheet v1.8*, Table 3-1. Strapping-pin behaviour is from Section 4 / Table 4-1 of the same document.

**Two hard constraints drove this allocation:**

1. **ADC2 is unusable while the radio is on.** Every analog input therefore lands on ADC1, which is GPIO1-GPIO10 only. There are 8 analog signals and 10 ADC1 channels, so the budget is tight by design.

2. **IO35/IO36/IO37 are only free on quad-PSRAM parts.** The datasheet reserves them for the Octal SPI PSRAM in the R8 and R16V variants. This board uses them, so **-N8R2 is mandatory** - do not substitute N8R8 or N16R8.

## Budget

- module pins accounted for: **39** (41 physical pads; GND@1, GND@40 and the EPAD share one row)
- signal pins in use: **36** (EN plus every GPIO)
- ADC1 channels carrying analog: **9 of 10** (1 more ADC1-capable pins are used digitally or held spare: `IO10`)
- ADC2 channels used for analog: **0** (deliberate - see above)
- strapping pins: `IO0` (boot button), `IO3` (spare, jumper is unpopulated), `IO45` (status LED), `IO46` (alert LED). The two LEDs are wired anode-to-GPIO / cathode-to-GND through a resistor, so at reset the pin is high-impedance, the LED does not conduct, and the internal weak pull-down holds the strap at its default 0.
- pin-JTAG (IO39-IO42) is given up so those four pins can carry signals; debugging uses the ESP32-S3's built-in USB-Serial-JTAG on IO19/IO20 instead.

## Free / reserved

Nothing is left floating. Every module pad is either driven, terminated, or brought to a test point - see ERC_REPORT.md.
